wave: CENSUS BLINDNESS -- the stack-overflow DoS guard was refusing to parse 9 of Atlas's own real, non-adversarial source files
wave_title: adapter::semantic::rust::max_structural_recursion_risk (the pre-syn::parse_file DoS guard, established across R4.3.5/R4.3.6/R4.3.7) had never been verified against this repository's own real, full source corpus. Direct re-census via `atlas-cli code analyze --root .` found 9 real files -- including runtime/src/census/mod.rs and core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs, files this session itself extensively modified -- tripping ResourceLimit and becoming completely invisible to semantic extraction (every dimension UNKNOWN), not from any adversarial input but from two genuine false-positive sources in the metric itself.

generation_model.G_n: b0f7d9fccb (fix(runtime): promote BUILD coverage in code_analyze's own census) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct re-census of this repository's own real state via `atlas-cli code analyze --root .`, inspecting the raw census.diagnostics array for anomalies (the same technique that found the prior generation's BUILD-coverage self-contradiction). Found 9 RESOURCE_LIMIT diagnostics naming real files this repository has always contained, none of them plausibly adversarial. Traced the exact false-positive mechanism by hand-tracing max_structural_recursion_risk's byte-scan logic against representative excerpts of the flagged files, then confirmed the hypothesis with a direct Python re-implementation of the scan run against the real file contents to locate the exact byte offset driving each file's maximum risk score -- found two independent root causes: (1) `,` counted cumulatively toward chain_run with no reset on ordinary identifier/whitespace bytes, so a long comma-separated argument/field list accumulated risk proportional to its length even though `syn` parses such lists iteratively, not recursively; (2) the scan has no comment or string-literal exclusion, so this codebase's own common `// --- section --------` dash-divider comment style, and a raw-string Cargo.lock test fixture, were themselves counted as dangerous operator runs.

priority_classification: census blindness (priority 4) bordering on correctness (priority 1) -- Atlas's own explicit standing directive requires census to include Atlas itself, and this guard was making that literally impossible for 9 real files, silently (each file still 'succeeds' in the sense of producing a ResourceLimit diagnostic rather than crashing, but every semantic dimension for it reads UNKNOWN, indistinguishable at a glance from a file that was never analyzed for a completely different reason). This is a self-inflicted blind spot in the census engine's own machinery, exactly the kind the standing loop's own directive names explicitly: 'the census engine must eventually census its own blind spots.'

design_decisions.question: For the comma false positive: exclude `,` from the counted operator set entirely, or make it a chain-resetting boundary (like `;`)?
design_decisions.decision: Reset chain_run on `,` (not remove it from consideration, not reset else_run). Reasoning: `,` in Rust syntax always separates independent SIBLING items in a list (function-call arguments, struct-literal fields, tuple elements, generic parameters, closure parameters) -- every one of these is parsed by `syn` via `Punctuated<T, Comma>`'s iterative loop, never via a call that recurses once per additional sibling. This is structurally analogous to why `;` already resets chain_run (a statement boundary), and unlike bracket nesting, chained binary operators, and if/else-if arms (all of which genuinely nest one AST level per occurrence), a comma-separated list adds O(1) stack depth regardless of length. Only chain_run resets, not else_run, because a `,` can legitimately appear inside one arm of a genuine if/else-if chain (e.g. a function call argument list inside an arm) without that arm's own commas being allowed to shorten the detected chain length -- the real if/else-chain vector must remain fully caught even when its arms contain ordinary comma-bearing code.

design_decisions.question: For the comment/string false positive: full syntax-aware tokenization, or targeted exclusion of just the two confirmed patterns?
design_decisions.decision: Targeted, scoped exclusion: skip `//` line comments (to end of line -- this codebase has zero `/* */` block comments, confirmed by direct grep across the whole workspace) and skip `"..."`/`r#"..."#`-style string literal content (with `\"` escape handling for plain strings and matching-hash-count handling for raw strings). Did NOT attempt char-literal (`'x'`) or byte-string (`b"..."`, `br"..."`) exclusion -- confirmed via direct inspection that none of the 9 real flagged files use either construct in a way that mattered, and the guard's own explicit, long-standing design principle ('may over-count, never under-count') means any remaining gap in string/char handling stays safe by construction, just possibly still conservative -- a smaller, honestly-scoped fix for what was actually reachable and demonstrated, not a rewrite into a full lexer.

design_decisions.question: Does excluding comment/string content risk weakening the guard against a real adversarial input that hides a chain inside what looks like a comment or string?
design_decisions.decision: No -- and this is provable, not merely asserted. Comment and string literal content is never fed to `syn::parse_file` as executable code either way (that is what makes it a comment or a string literal); removing it from the risk SCAN can only ever lower a computed risk score relative to the unfixed scan, it can never cause a genuine code-level chain (which necessarily lives outside any comment or string, since it must be real Rust syntax syn will actually parse) to be missed. Added a dedicated regression test (`a_real_adversarial_chain_after_a_comment_still_trips_the_guard`) proving a real 5,000-term chain elsewhere in the same file is still caught even when the file also contains an ordinary preceding comment.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: An ordinary long comma-separated argument/field list, a decorative comment divider, and dashes inside a raw string literal are never treated as recursion-DoS risk; all three originally-confirmed adversarial vectors (bracket nesting, chained binary operators, if/else-if chains) are still caught with zero weakening, including when they co-occur with an unrelated preceding comment.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Four new tests in adapter/src/semantic/rust/tests.rs: a_long_comma_separated_argument_list_does_not_trip_the_recursion_guard, a_long_decorative_comment_divider_does_not_trip_the_recursion_guard, a_raw_string_literal_containing_dashes_does_not_trip_the_recursion_guard (all three run against the unfixed code first and confirmed to fail with a real ResourceLimit diagnostic before either fix was written), and a_real_adversarial_chain_after_a_comment_still_trips_the_guard (regression guard). All three pre-existing adversarial-vector tests (deeply_nested_parenthesized_expression_does_not_abort_the_process, long_bracket_free_binary_operator_chain_does_not_abort_the_process, long_if_else_chain_does_not_abort_the_process) and their three matching 'short real X still extracts normally' companions re-run unchanged and pass.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Re-ran `atlas-cli code analyze --root .` against this repository's own real, full source corpus (not a synthetic fixture -- the actual production files this session has read and edited throughout): RESOURCE_LIMIT diagnostics dropped from 9 to 0, and INCOMPLETE_ANALYSIS diagnostics (the honest 'partial coverage' signal, expected and correct) rose from 407 to 464, confirming these 9 files are now genuinely being walked and analyzed rather than silently reporting UNKNOWN for every dimension. `atlas-cli systemize`, `check`, and `docs audit` all re-run clean with zero regression -- coding_admission remains fully green (allowed: true, zero blockers, the milestone reached two generations ago).

overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. Closed a real, live census-blindness gap in Atlas's own semantic-extraction machinery: the stack-overflow DoS guard was refusing to parse 9 of Atlas's own real, non-adversarial source files -- exactly the kind of self-inflicted blind spot the standing loop's own directive requires the census engine to eventually find in itself. Root-caused to two independent false-positive sources (comma-counted-as-chain; no comment/string exclusion), both fixed with a provable, non-weakening safety argument, and verified both syntehtically (falsification-first regression tests) and against this repository's own real, complete source corpus (9 -> 0 false positives, with genuinely increased real coverage, not merely a suppressed count).
